story_title: A Day at the Blacksmith's Workshop
paragraphs: A group of students visits a blacksmith's workshop to learn how metal objects are made. The blacksmith, Mara, {{mask_1}} them that the workshop is an active work area. She {{mask_2}}, "Please stand behind the yellow line." Her assistant {{mask_3}} the students to keep their bags away from the workbench. One student {{mask_4}} that the room smelled like warm metal.

Mara explains the tools before starting a demonstration. She {{mask_5}} the students that the metal must be heated before it can be shaped. Then she {{mask_6}} to the group, "Watch how I use the hammer." Her assistant {{mask_7}} them to wear protective glasses. A student {{mask_8}} Mara that the safety glasses felt comfortable.

During the demonstration, Mara heats a small piece of steel. She {{mask_9}}, "The metal changes color as it gets hotter." The assistant {{mask_10}} the visitors that they should stay in the marked area. A student {{mask_11}} to her friend that the hammer looked heavier than it was. Mara {{mask_12}} the group that each tool had a special purpose.

After the demonstration, the students ask about the finished objects. Mara {{mask_13}} them that blacksmiths can make gates, hooks, and decorative pieces. She {{mask_14}} to a student, "You can ask me about the design." The student {{mask_15}} Mara that she wanted to learn how to make a small hook. The assistant {{mask_16}} the class that they could see examples on the display table.

Before the visit ends, Mara shows the group a finished iron flower. She {{mask_17}}, "I made this design for the town garden." The teacher {{mask_18}} the students that it was time to return to school. One student {{mask_19}} to Mara, "Thank you for showing us your workshop." Mara {{mask_20}} them that they were welcome to visit again.
